answer.new_information: NVIDIA announced on 2026-07-01 a new business model in which AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure for AI-native, enterprise and ISV customers under a revenue-sharing and credit-support model. NVIDIA says it will earn standard product revenue plus a share of cloud revenue on supported capacity. No dollar amounts, credit-support size, revenue-share percentage, term, or number of partners are given. Sharon AI and Firmus quotes and the Firmus Batam campus (360 MW, up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs) are company-sourced plans with no timeline or delivery confirmation. The item is NVIDIA's own statement, so it is not independent evidence of demand or of the economics.
answer.new_question: How large is NVIDIA's credit-support and revenue-share exposure to AI cloud partners under the new model, and how much of its revenue and receivables depend on these arrangements?
answer.independent_judgement: The announcement adds a possible investment judgement not covered by the current catalog: NVIDIA is moving from selling hardware to sharing cloud revenue and providing credit support for partner capacity. That could add recurring, usage-linked earnings, but it also puts NVIDIA's balance sheet behind partners' financing, adds counterparty and concentration risk, and can make part of reported demand circular. Whether this changes the position depends on disclosed amounts, terms, and whether partner capacity is actually built and utilised. Until those are disclosed, treat the model as a strategic change with unquantified risk, not as a proven earnings stream.
answer.reason: The record is a company announcement of a new commercial structure with credit support and revenue sharing. It is a potentially position-relevant decision with no catalog questions or stored pieces to update, so it is proposed as a new question. The Sharon AI, Firmus and DSX-factory items are relays or plans from the same NVIDIA release, not separate evidence, and they move no numbers yet.
